evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_tools.py::test_search_models_rejects_limit_over_hard_cap -v -> PASSED; respx route.called asserted False (2026-11-04, commit 48f25fc)

text: Given repo_id="bert-base-uncased", when huggingface_get_model is called, then it returns the model's tags/pipeline_tag/license/siblings count
Given a repo_id that does not exist, when huggingface_get_model is called, then it returns not_found, not a raw 404 passthrough or a 500
Given query="imdb", when huggingface_search_datasets is called, then matching datasets are returned with the documented fields
Given a nonexistent dataset repo_id, when huggingface_get_dataset is called, then it returns not_found
Given query="gradio", when huggingface_search_spaces is called, then matching Spaces are returned including sdk and stage
Given a nonexistent Space repo_id, when huggingface_get_space is called, then it returns not_found
Given a valid token, when huggingface_whoami is called, then it returns the token owner's name/type/orgs
steps: Export a real Hugging Face read-scope token as HF_TOKEN
expect: 200 response whose result contains name, type (user|org), and an orgs array (possibly empty)
notes: needs a real vendor account (no shared HF test token on this queue); not a blocker per vendor-mcp-development SOP "no test account" rule. Tool implementation and routing verified via local docker smoke test (placeholder token -> 200, tool present in tools/list).

text: Given a syntactically-present but invalid/expired token, when huggingface_whoami is called, then it returns unauthorized (mapped from the Hub's 401), not a raw exception or 500
expect: Tool result is the structured error envelope with code=unauthorized, retryable=false; HTTP transport itself still returns 200 (MCP-level error, not transport 401 -- the 401 in AC10 is specifically for the *missing* header case)
notes: needs a real vendor account to obtain a token shape the Hub will actually reject with 401 rather than a malformed-token 400; not a blocker. The 401/403->unauthorized mapping itself is covered by classify_status, exercised indirectly by the mocked-transport error-mapping tests (test_get_model_maps_404_to_not_found and siblings exercise the same client._to_error/classify_status path for 404; the 401/403 branches use the identical code path).

text: Given a token for an account with zero repos of a given repo_type, when huggingface_list_owned_repos is called, then it returns an empty items list, not not_found
steps: Use a real token for an account (or a freshly created one) with no datasets
expect: result is {"items": [], "has_more": false}, not an error
notes: needs a real vendor account; not a blocker. Code path (empty list from the Hub API -> empty items, no not_found branch exists in huggingface_list_owned_repos) reviewed by inspection: the tool never raises not_found for an empty author-scoped listing, only for upstream HTTP errors.

text: Given an existing public repo_id and its default revision, when huggingface_list_repo_files is called, then it returns the file tree with path/size for each entry
Given an existing repo_id but a nonexistent revision, when huggingface_list_repo_files is called, then it returns not_found
Given a valid token, a provider-served model, and a one-turn messages list, when huggingface_run_inference is called, then it returns generated text and a finish_reason
steps: Export a real HF token with inference access as HF_TOKEN
Call huggingface_run_inference with model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct", messages=[{role:user, content:"Say hi in one word"}]
expect: result contains a non-empty text field and a finish_reason (e.g. "stop")
notes: needs a real vendor account with inference-provider access; not a blocker. Response-shape mapping (choices[0].message.content -> text, finish_reason, usage) reviewed by inspection against the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions schema; exercised structurally by test_run_inference_maps_503_to_upstream_error/429 for the error path.

text: Given a model that is currently loading/unavailable on every provider, when huggingface_run_inference is called, then it returns upstream_error with retryable: true, not a raw 503
steps: Call huggingface_run_inference against a model known to be cold/rarely served, or simulate via a provider that returns 503 with estimated_time
expect: result is the error envelope with code=upstream_error, retryable=true
notes: needs a real vendor account; provider cold-start timing is not reliably reproducible without one. The mapping logic itself is now covered by an auto unit test added by the dev leg, see TC-HGF-016-AUTO.

text: Given the Inference Providers router returns 503 (model loading) on every retry attempt, when huggingface_run_inference is called, then it returns upstream_error with retryable:true
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_tools.py::test_run_inference_maps_503_to_upstream_error -v -> PASSED (2026-11-04, commit 48f25fc). Added per the note on TC-HGF-016 asking the dev leg to cover the mapping logic with a mocked-transport unit test.

text: Given the Inference Providers router returns 429 on every retry attempt, when huggingface_run_inference is called, then it returns rate_limited with retryable:true

text: Given a valid Write-scope token and an existing, not-yet-liked repo, when huggingface_like_repo is called twice in a row, then both calls succeed and the second call does not error or create a duplicate like
steps: Export a real HF token with Write scope as HF_TOKEN
Call huggingface_like_repo on a model repo_id not yet liked by that account, twice in a row
expect: both calls return {"liked": true}; the Hub shows exactly one like from that account afterwards
notes: needs a real vendor account with a Write-scope token; not a blocker. huggingface_like_repo always returns {"liked": true} on any 2xx POST /like response and never branches on prior-liked state, matching the Hub's own documented idempotent like endpoint behavior (reviewed by inspection, not live-verified).

text: Given a nonexistent repo_id, when huggingface_like_repo is called, then it returns not_found
steps: Call huggingface_like_repo with a repo_id that does not exist on the Hub
expect: result is the error envelope with code=not_found
notes: needs a real vendor account (the like endpoint requires auth before it will even evaluate whether the repo exists); not a blocker. Error-mapping path is the same classify_status(404)->not_found path exercised by TC-HGF-005/007/009.

text: Given a tool call with no X-Huggingface-Token header, when any tool is called, then the server returns 401 naming the required header, before any outbound Hugging Face call is made
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_middleware.py::test_missing_header_returns_401_before_any_outbound_call -v -> PASSED (2026-11-04, commit 48f25fc). Also confirmed live in the built container: curl -i -X POST http://localhost:18099/mcp (no header) -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized, body {"error":"Missing credentials","message":"Missing required header: X-Huggingface-Token","required_headers":["X-Huggingface-Token"]} (2026-11-04, image sha256:7c800ce9379d)

text: Given two concurrent requests carrying token A and token B respectively, when both call huggingface_whoami at the same time, then request A's response never contains token B's identity or vice versa
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_middleware.py::test_concurrent_requests_with_different_tokens_never_cross -v -> PASSED, full ASGI round trip with two concurrent /mcp calls and distinct mocked whoami-v2 responses per Authorization header; each response verified to contain only its own tenant's name and not the other's (2026-11-04, commit 48f25fc)

text: Given the service running locally with a mocked Hugging Face backend, when 10 concurrent huggingface_search_models calls are sustained for 30 seconds, then the P95 latency added by the MCP layer itself is <= 500ms and no response contains another concurrent request's data
steps: Run the service locally with the upstream Hugging Face client swapped for a mocked transport with a fixed 50ms simulated latency
Run a load tool (e.g. hey or a small asyncio script) at 10 concurrent requests sustained for 30s against POST /mcp tools/call huggingface_search_models, using a distinct token per logical client
Record per-request latency and subtract the mocked backend's fixed 50ms to isolate the MCP layer's own overhead
Assert every response's items correspond only to that request's own token/query combination
expect: P95 of (observed latency - 50ms mocked backend latency) <= 500ms; zero cross-request data contamination
notes: operational load test; not executed in this round (no load-test harness set up in this environment). Cross-request isolation itself (the correctness half of this AC) is already covered by TC-HGF-021's concurrent-request test, which uses the real middleware/contextvar path, not a simulation; only the latency/load dimension remains unverified. Not a blocker per SOP -- flagged for a follow-up pass with a real load tool if P95 latency becomes a concern in production.
